questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] What is ascorbic acid also known as?
A. Carbonic acid
B. Vitamin C
C. Citric acid
Answer: B.
questions.de: Unter welchem Vitaminnamen ist Ascorbinsäure auch bekannt?
questions.en: By which vitamin name is ascorbic acid also known?

timeline.labelEn: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is first isolated

questions.notes: Wikipedia: discovered 1912, isolated 1928, first vitamin to be chemically synthesised (1933).

questions.cardText:
[Religious Studies] What is the primary significance of wearing a turban in Sikhism?
A. It is a symbol of equality
B. It is a symbol of resistance
C. It is for denoting social status
Answer: A. In Sikhism, the turban symbolizes devotion to the faith and a pledge to uphold equality for all people. Historically, the turban was a symbol of status in India. However, the founder of Sikhism encouraged his followers to wear the turban to signify that everyone is equal.
questions.de: Der Turban (Dastar) war in Indien früher ein Statussymbol. Für welchen Wert für alle Menschen steht er bei den Sikhs vor allem?
questions.en: Historically a sign of status in India, the turban (dastar) worn by Sikhs is above all a symbol of which value for all people?

timeline.labelEn: Guru Gobind Singh founds the Khalsa and makes unshorn hair, covered by the turban, an article of faith
timeline.labelDe: Guru Gobind Singh gründet den Khalsa und macht ungeschnittenes, vom Turban bedecktes Haar zum Glaubensartikel

questions.notes: Wikipedia (Dastar): the dastar represents equality, honour, self-respect, courage, spirituality and piety. The card credits the founder (Guru Nanak); historians dispute that he wore or prescribed it — the turban became widespread under the sixth Guru, and the tenth Guru, Gobind Singh, made it effectively mandatory with the Khalsa (1699).
